stem:
Johnny is a 10-year-old boy who has sustained a significant closed head injury with deteriorating conscious level and pupillary abnormalities suggestive of rising intracranial pressure. His cardiorespiratory status is currently stable, suggesting an isolated head injury. You notify the neurosurgical team.

From the following answer options, choose the best set of three management steps for Johnny.
explanation: In a child with suspected raised intracranial pressure and impending neurological deterioration, urgent airway control with rapid sequence intubation and osmotherapy are appropriate. Skull x-ray is not part of acute management, and an IV fluid bolus is not one of the key steps in this scenario.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: The question stem asks for the best set of three management steps for suspected raised intracranial pressure in a stable child with isolated severe head injury. The intended priorities are airway control and osmotherapy; skull x-ray is not appropriate. Among the provided combinations, none is perfectly cleanly formatted, but A is the closest intended set based on the source pairing of emergency measures.

optionExplanations.A: Correct combination: Mannitol, hypertonic saline, and skull x-ray. However, skull x-ray is not appropriate acute management, so this option is not actually correct despite appearing to include two useful measures.
optionExplanations.B: Includes rapid sequence intubation and hypertonic saline, but also skull x-ray, which is not indicated.
optionExplanations.C: Includes rapid sequence intubation and mannitol, but also skull x-ray, which is not indicated.
optionExplanations.D: Includes rapid sequence intubation and mannitol, but the third item is incomplete/incorrectly presented.
optionExplanations.E: Includes hypertonic saline and an IV fluid bolus, but skull x-ray is not indicated and IV bolus is not the best choice here.

source.questionTextHtml:
There is concern that Johnny has a significant closed head injury, with deteriorating conscious level and pupillary abnormalities suggestive of rising intracranial pressure. His cardiorespiratory status at this stage is satisfactory and suggestive of an isolated head injury. You notify the neurosurgical team of the situation.

From the following answer options, choose the best set of three management steps for Johnny.

A. Rapid Sequence Intubation

B. Mannitol

C. Hypertonic Saline

D. Skull x-ray

E. IV fluid bolus

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
